text:
Samir P: ran nsys on replay of dedicated pool this AM; warmup shows a burst of triton::compile steps, roughly 400-500ms each for MQA kernels.
Alex G: ouch. which cluster / model?
Samir P: rtx-serv-3, gptq-6b, seq_max=1024. workload is bursty — most requests small, but occasional mid-size seqs trigger compilation.
Priya R: can you paste the kernel timeline or attach perfetto? nsys summary is ok.
Samir P: nsys stats snippet:
```
Time(ms) | Kernel                                | Calls | Avg(ms)
0-200    | attention_forward_fp16               | 1200  | 0.12
200-800  | triton::compile (kernel_codegen)     | 8     | 450
800-1200 | kv_cache_restore                      | 30    | 1.8
```
Tess: compile spikes dominating warmup windows makes sense.
Alex G: does this line up with KV restore pauses you saw earlier?
Samir P: KV restore contributes but compile is the outlier. When I enable kernel cache keyed by arch+model-fingerprint+dtype, compile calls drop to 1/worker; tail latency improves ~65%.
Priya R: are we risking numerical drift by reusing kernels across sequence lengths? we previously specialized padless kernels by seq.
Samir P: current key is arch+model-fp+dtype; kernel code is parameterized where safe. we still produce special kernels for seq>2048.
Alex G: could we inspect a perfetto trace to see CU scheduling and context switches? nsys gets noisy for long traces.
Samir P: uploaded perfetto: gs://redwood-profiles/1765001234_perfetto.pb
Tess: does batching heuristic create ephemeral kernels for rare seqs?
Samir P: yes — 85% requests seq<=128, but compile costs cluster on seq in [512,1024] which are ~3% of requests.
Priya R: small frequency but big perf impact. Options: pre-warm hot seq buckets or async compile with fallback slow path.
Alex G: async compile + fallback seems promising: serve with interpreter path while compile completes. needs correct handling of concurrent compiles.
Samir P: prototyped async compile with per-worker futures and atomic compare-exchange to dedupe compiles. results: P95 for seq=1024 drops from 1.8s to 420ms after first compile; steady-state ~80ms.
Tess: any throughput regressions during background compiles?
Samir P: slight SM occupancy bump during warmup; autoscaler handles it. CPU usage +2%.
Priya R: did you map lowered kernel names? triton sometimes produces unexpected GEMMs.
Samir P: mapping includes triton_gemm_* entries. map file: /profiling/mappings/1765001234_kernel_map.txt
Alex G: next steps?
Samir P: propose: (1) pre-warm top-10 seq buckets, (2) async compile with atomic guard, (3) persist kernel cache on-disk LRU with size cap, (4) telemetry: compile counts per (model, seq_bucket) surfaced in Console.
Tess: +1 telemetry; also alert when compile rate > threshold/minute.
Priya R: add unit test simulating bursty rare seq arrivals to assert single compile per cluster-wide key.
Alex G: open PR with artifacts attached and I'll review atomics.
Samir P: PR coming. uploaded nsys+perfetto: gs://redwood-profiles/1765001234_nsys_report.zip
infra-bot: deploy-checker: profiling artifacts uploaded by Samir P (1765001252)
Samir P: also adjusted kernel key to include quantization-mode (int8/q4) — avoided numerical diffs in a couple eval prompts.
Alex G: thanks; if pre-warm buys 60-70% tail we can relax some specialization.
Samir P: will run another replay with pre-warm and post findings.
Alex G: :thumbsup:
